about: The shared vocabulary of skill libraries: every term a skill's metadata header or a search request may use. Each group names the header field and the request field that take its terms. docs/skill-library-vocabulary.md maps each criterion of plugin/assign/table.json to these terms and gives the rules that rex skills check applies.

terms.about: Standards for how a type of work must be done.
A way of working for one activity.
How to use one named technology.
Material to look things up in.
How code must be written: naming, types, comments, errors, layout, dependencies, failure handling, language gaps.
How to test, and the rules for each type of test.
Work before code: sketches, validation plans, spikes, priorities.
Finding and fixing problems in existing code.
Speed and resource use.
Checking someone else's plan or change.
Diagrams and visual documentation.
Writing skills, prompts and briefs for agents.
The task writes or changes code.
The languages of the task's code, as rex codebase --only names them.
The role of the agent the request is for, as the plan names it, such as plan-reviewer.
Paths of files present in the repo, relative to its root, such as Cargo.toml.
Names of the packages the repo depends on, as its manifests name them.
The time budget of the task's hot path: ns_us is nanoseconds to tens of microseconds, ms is milliseconds or slower. Left out when the task names no budget.
The skill applies only to a task whose writes_code is one of the listed values.
The skill applies only to code in one of the listed languages.
The skill applies only to a hot path of one of the listed time budgets.
Builds a new feature.
Fixes a bug.
Changes the structure of code without changing what it does.
Designs a system, feature or module before its code.
Reviews a branch or pull request that it wrote none of.
Audits existing code for problems.
Writes or changes tests and no other code.
Writes or changes documentation, not code.
A test replaces an outside API or database, the file system, time or randomness with a stand-in.
Creates, splits or moves a code file, module or code folder, and decides where it goes. A folder of skill text or documents is not code.
Adds or upgrades a dependency.
Handles input from outside the program.
Keeps long-running state, or writes a main loop.
Retries an operation or reconnects to a service.
Rests on an approach, crate or outside service that is not proven.
Refactors code that is old or that the agent does not know.
Finds friction or refactor candidates in the module structure of existing code.
A decision that depends on a ranking of qualities.
Starts a sub-agent of the job and writes its brief.
Threads, locks and work shared between cores.
Memory allocation and its cost.
How long one operation takes, including its tail.
How easily a person reads and changes the code.
An inline unit test of a pure function, kept only until a contract or integration test covers the same code.
A test of the interface between two modules.
A test of an invariant that must always hold, or a property test.
A test against the real outside world: an API, an exchange, a database or a WebSocket.
A diagram in a plan or document.
The plan of a code plan job.
A skill, a prompt or agent instructions.
A brief for another agent.
